reason: The sources provide 16 multi-sourced claims detailing the void's discovery, massive scale, and controversial link to the multiverse.
story: In 2004, astronomers scanning the Big Bang’s afterglow discovered a massive anomaly: a 'Cold Spot' in the constellation Eridanus. This was the Eridanus Supervoid, a region of space spanning up to two billion light-years that is almost entirely empty. It isn't a black hole; it is a vast wasteland mostly devoid of stars, gas, and even invisible dark matter. As ancient light photons cross this vacuum, the universe’s expansion stretches the void, causing the light to lose energy and appear colder—a process called the Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect. While some scientists think it is a statistical fluke, others propose a mind-bending alternative: the Cold Spot might be a 'bruise' caused by our universe colliding with a parallel one. Whether it is an impossible emptiness or a mark from another dimension, this 'Axis of Evil' challenges our fundamental understanding of the cosmic web.
angle: Scientists believe a massive, billion-light-year hole in space could be the bruise left by a collision with a parallel universe.

claims.claim: The Eridanus Supervoid was discovered in 2004.
The void is located in the direction of the constellation Eridanus.
It is associated with an unusually large 'Cold Spot' in the Cosmic Microwave Background radiation.
The Cold Spot is approximately 70 microkelvin cooler than the average cosmic background temperature.
The supervoid spans a distance between one and two billion light-years across.
The region is largely devoid of normal matter like stars and gas.
The void is also strangely empty of invisible dark matter.
The cooling of light as it crosses the void is known as the Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect.
Photons lose energy when traversing the void because the universe's expansion stretches the region while they cross it.
The anomaly was first detected using data from NASA's WMAP satellite.
The European Space Agency's Planck satellite confirmed the anomaly's existence in 2013.
The structure is sometimes referred to as the 'Great Void'.
The anomaly has been nicknamed the 'Axis of Evil' because it was unexpected in current cosmological models.
Some researchers theorize the Cold Spot is an imprint of a collision with a parallel universe.
The Dark Energy Survey (DES) confirmed the presence of a significant under-density in the area using luminous red galaxies.
A 2015 study by Istvan Szapudi mapped the region using the Pan-STARRS1 telescope and the WISE satellite.

disputed: The exact distance to the void (studies suggest it is 3 billion light-years away, while others place it 6 to 10 billion light-years away).
The exact width of the void (ranging from nearly one billion to two billion light-years).
The physical structure (some 2017 surveys suggest multiple smaller voids instead of one massive supervoid).
The angular size on the sky (reported as 10 degrees wide in some data and over 30 degrees in others).
The temperature drop (measured as 70 microkelvin by most, but some assessments report up to 150 millionths of a degree).
